title: Vectorized Conditional Selection
subtopics: Choosing Between Scalar and Vectorized Conditions
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of vectorized conditional selection and identify its main inputs, outputs or constraints.
Apply ifelse() in a minimal example and state the expected result before checking it.
Test one relevant edge, missing or failure case and describe a limitation of the result.

content.intro: Vectorized Conditional Selection is part of Conditions, Loops, and Control Flow. Start with ifelse() and connect it to the worked example and expected result.
content.why_it_matters: R works naturally with vectors, so indexing and vectorized operations can transform many values without a manual loop.

content_blocks.title: Why this matters
content_blocks.text: R works naturally with vectors, so indexing and vectorized operations can transform many values without a manual loop. The example is intentionally small so you can predict its result before checking it in a local R session.

items.title: ifelse()
items.text: Explain ifelse() in the context of vectorized conditional selection, connect it to the example, and verify one expected result or edge case.

items.title: Choosing Between Scalar and Vectorized Conditions
items.text: Compare choosing between scalar and vectorized conditions using concrete trade-offs, assumptions and maintenance needs; state when each choice is appropriate.

items.title: Handling Missing Conditions
items.text: For handling missing conditions, include a failing or boundary case and explain how it should be detected without silently losing information.

items.title: Avoiding Type and Recycling Surprises
items.text: Explain avoiding type and recycling surprises in the context of vectorized conditional selection, connect it to the example, and verify one expected result or edge case.

content_blocks.title: Work through it
content_blocks.text: Predict the output length and selected positions, then test a value on the condition boundary. Change one input or condition at a time, compare the observed result with your prediction, and write down one limitation.

content_blocks.title: R example: Vectorized Conditional Selection
content_blocks.code:
# Lesson 51: Vectorized Conditional Selection
example_values <- 4:7
example_values[example_values > 5]

content_blocks.limitations: The logical index keeps values above a visible threshold; check the boundary and result length. Verify the snippet and expected output with the supported R and package versions before publishing.

content_blocks.title: Common pitfall
content_blocks.text: Do not treat a syntactically plausible example as proof of correctness. For vectorized conditional selection, check the input type, missing/empty cases, output shape, and domain assumptions.

common_mistakes.problem: Using an example without checking its inputs or output shape.
common_mistakes.why: R can coerce types, propagate missing values or simplify results unexpectedly.
common_mistakes.fix: Inspect with str(), class(), typeof(), length() or dim() and add a direct check.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating a demonstration as proof that every edge case works.
common_mistakes.why: Empty input, missing values, dependencies and version differences can change behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Test a normal case and a boundary/failure case in a clean local R session.

common_mistakes.why: The conclusion depends on data provenance, transformations and assumptions.
common_mistakes.fix: Record input source, cleaning choices and known limitations beside the result.
